report has been filed with the stock exc/hanges and is available on the ~ompany's website.
As per Ind AS 108 - 'Operating Segments', the Company has reported segment infonnation under two segments I.e. 1) Transmission Equipment and 2) Material Handling Equipment (MHE).
Revenue from Operations and Other Income includes income for INR 2,529 lakhs and INR 975 lakhs respectively on account of settlement or arbitration claims against customers of MHE division
during the quarter ended on 30th June, 2025.
The Board of Directors declared an interim dividend of )NR 0.50/- per equity share of !NR 1/- each. The record date for the payment is 21st October, 2026.
Eimco Elecon (India) Ltd. ceased to be an Associate effective 23rd April, 2025 and hence had been reclassified as financial asset with reporting at fair valued at each reporting date In accord.ance
with Ind AS109. Accordingly, unrealised mark to market gain of INR 14,942 lakhs (net of tax) fi ll the date or tennination has been credited to Statement of Profit and Loss and considered as an
exceptional item in the half year ending on 30th September, 2025 . After the date of tennination, Unrealised gain/loss of the respective periods has been included in the Other Compre hensive
Income in accordance with one time irrevocable option available under Ind AS.
Previous period figures have been regrouped I reclassified wherever necessary. Amounts reported are ln INR Lakhs and are based on the actual amounts, and therefore, the sum of the
components may not equal the total amount reported In INR Lakhs due to rounding. .

Independent Auditor's Review Report on Quarterly Unaudited and Year to Date Standalone Financial
Results of Elecon Engineering Company Limited pursuant to the Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended.
To
The Board of Directors of
Elecon Engineering Company Limited
1. We have reviewed the accompanying Statement of Unaudited Standalone Financial Results of Elecon
Engineerin g Com p any Limited ("the Company") for the quarter ende d 3 0th September 2026 and year to
date result fo r the period 1st April, 2026 t o 30th Sep temb er, 2026, ("the Statement"), attached herewith, being
submitted by the Co mpany p ursuant to the requirement of Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations
and Disclos w. e Rt<:luiremen:rs) Regulations, 2015, as amended (' Listmg Regulations");
2. Thi s Scatem.ent, which is the res p o~ ib ility o f th e Company's Managemen t and a pproved by the Company's
Board of Dir ectors, has been pre pared in acc ordance with the xe cognition and .measurement principles laid
down in Indian Accouot:ing Standa rd 34 "Interim Financial Rep or ting" (" Ind AS 34"), pxescribed under:
Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 ('the A ct ') as amended, read with relevant rules issued thereund er
and other accounting principles gene.rally accepted in In dia and in compliance with Regulation 33 of the Listing
Regulations. Our xesp onsibility is to express a conclusion on the Statement based on our review;
3. We conducted CUI review of the Statement in. accordance with the Standard on Review Engagements (SRE)
2410 ''Review oflaterim Financial Information Performed by the Ind ependent Auditor of the Entity", issued
by the In stitute of Chartered Accountants oflndia . 'Ibis standard requires that we plan and perform the review
to obtain moderate asslirance as to whe th er the stateme nt is free of material misstatement. A review of interim
financial information consists of making inquiries, primarily of persons responsible for financial and
accounting matt ers, and applying analytical a nd other review procedures. A review is substantially less in scope
than an audit conduc ted -in ac cord ance wi th Standards on Auditing and consequently does not enable us to
obtain assurance that we wo uld beco me a.ware of all significant matters that might be identified in an audit.
Accordingly, we do not express an audit opinion;
4. Based on our review conducted as above, nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe that the
accompanying Statement prepared .in accordance with recognition and measurement principles laid down in
the aforesaid Indian Accounting Standards prescribed under section 133 of the Act read with relevant rules
issued thereunder and other accounting principles generally accepted in India, has not disclosed the
information required to be disclosed 41 terms of the Listing Regulations, including the manner in which, it is
to be disclosed, or that it contains any material misstatement.

Independent Auditor's Review Report on Unaudited Quarterly and Year to Date Consolidated Financial
Results of Elecon Engineering Con;1.pany Limited pursuant to the Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 as amended.
To
The Board of Directors of
Elecon Engineering Company Limited
1. We have reviewed the accompanying Statement of Unaudited Consolidated Financial Results of Elecon
Engineering Company Limited (hereinafter referred to as the 'the Holding Company") and its subsidiaries (the
Holding Company and its subsidiaries together referred to as "the Group") for the quarter ended 30th September
2026 and year to date result for the' period 1st April, 2026 to 30th September, 2026 ("the Statement''), attached
herewith, being submitted by the Holding Company pursuant to the requirement of Regulation 33 of the SEBI
(Llsting Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended ("Listing Regulations");
2. This Statement, which is the responsibility of the Holding Company's Management and approved by the Holding
Company's Board of Directors, has been prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement
principles laid down in the Indian Accounting Standard 34 "Interim Financial Reporting" ("Ind AS 34"),
prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 ('the Act') as amended, read with relevant rules issued
thereunder and other accounting principles generally accepted in India and in compliance with Regulation 33 of
the Listing Regulations. Our responsibility is to express a conclusion on the Statement based on our review;
3. We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagements (SRE) 2410
''Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the Entity", issued by the
Institute of Chartered Accountants oflndia. This standard requires that we plan and perform the review to obtain
moderate assurance as to whether the statement is free of material misstatement. A review of interim financial
information consists of making inquiries, primarily of persons responsible for financial and accounting matters,
and applying analytical and other review procedures. A review is substantially less in scope than an audit
conducted in accordance with Standards on Auditing and consequently does not enable us to obtain assurance
that we would become aware of all. significant matters that might be identified in an audit. Accordingly, we do
not express an audit opinion;
We also performed procedures in accordance with the circular issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of
India under Regulation 33 (8) of the Listing Regulations, to the extent applicable;
4. The Statement includes the results of the entities as mentioned in the Annexure enclosed herewith.
5. Based on our review conducted and procedures performed stated in paragraph 3 above, and based on the
consideration of review reports of Subsidiaries' auditors referred to in paragraph 6 below, nothing has come to
our attention that causes us to believe that the accompanying Statement, prepared in accordance with recognition
and measurement principles laid down in the aforesaid Indian Accounting Standards specified under Section 133
of the Act as amended, read with relevant rules issued thereunder and other accounting principles generally
accepted in India, has not disclosed the information required to be disclosed in terms of the Listing Regulations,
including the manner in which it is to be disclosed; or that it contains any material misstatement.

its unaudited Financial Result for the quarter & half-year ended 30th September 2026.

-- 17 of 20 --

Gear Division
Our Gear division continued to deliver strong growth in Q2 FY27, with revenue increasing 10.6% Y-o-Y to ₹488
crores driven by disciplined execution, reinforcing the division’s strong contribution to our consolidated
performance.
EBIT for the quarter increased 27.2% Y-o-Y to ₹108 crores, while the EBIT margin expanded by 290 bps to 22.1%.
The margin improvement was driven by outpacing in revenue growth, a favourable revenue mix, and supported by
operating leverage.
Order intake remained broadly stable at ₹493 crores during Q2, while H1 order intake grew 8.8% to ₹1,063 crores.
Our open order book increased 37.0% Y-o-Y to ₹1,056 crores, providing healthy revenue visibility.
MHE Division
The MHE division registered a revenue growth of 10.4% Y-o-Y during Q2 FY27. While project execution improved
compared to Q1, a further acceleration in execution is anticipated during the remainder of H2 FY27.
The moderation in EBIT margin was primarily attributable to unfavorable product mix, increased input costs, and
operating deleverage resulting from lower scale of operations on account of delayed clearances for the projects.
Order momentum remained strong, with intake growing 32.5% to ₹253 crores in Q2, supported by overseas orders
of ₹68 crores.
The open order book increased 27.3% Y-o-Y to ₹579 crores, providing healthy execution visibility.

-- 18 of 20 --

Commenting on the results, Mr. Prayasvin B. Patel, Chairman & Managing Director of
Elecon Engineering Company Ltd. said,
“Q2 FY27 marked another quarter of healthy performance for Elecon, with Consolidated Revenue
growing 10.5% Y-o-Y to ₹639 crores, while EBITDA increased 17.7% to ₹148 crores. EBITDA margin
expanded by 140 bps to 23.1%, supported by a higher contribution from the gear division, driven by
disciplined execution and the ability to maintain operations through challenges. Profit After Tax stood
at ₹96 crores, with a PAT margin of 15.1%. For H1 FY27, revenue stood at ₹1,160 crores, representing
11.1% growth over adjusted H1 FY26, while adjusted EBITDA grew 11.4% to ₹257 crores with a margin
of 22.2%.
Our Gear Division continued to drive growth, with Q2 revenue increasing 10.6% Y-o-Y to ₹488 crores
and EBIT growing 27.2% to ₹108 crores, resulting in an improved EBIT margin of 22.1%. The division
also maintained healthy momentum during H1 FY27, with revenue increasing 13.1% and EBIT growing
21.8%. The open order book for the division stood at ₹1,056 crores, providing a strong executable
backlog. The Material Handling Equipment (MHE) Division reported Q2 revenue of ₹151 crores,
registering growth of 10.4% Y-o-Y. However, EBIT margin moderated to 20.2%, due to an unfavorable
product mix, and slower project execution. Encouragingly, MHE order intake grew 32.5% Y-o-Y to ₹253
crores, including overseas orders of ₹68 crores, while the open order book increased 27.3% to ₹579
crores.
Our overseas business, comprising exports and overseas subsidiaries, continued to gain momentum,
with revenue reaching ₹159 crores during Q2 FY27, and registering 30.6% Y-o-Y growth. While global
macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties persist, we remain focused on strengthening our reach
across international markets.
Our consolidated order intake increased 8.4% Y-o-Y to ₹746 crores during Q2 FY27 and 15.3% to
₹1,501 crores during H1 FY27. The consolidated open order book stood at ₹1,635 crores as of 30th
September 2026, up approximately 33% Y-o-Y, with healthy contributions from both divisions. Our
robust order book not only provides strong revenue visibility but also reinforces our confidence in
continuing to be the preferred choice of our customers.
As we mark 75 years of Elecon, we remain focused on strengthening our leadership in industrial gear
solutions and material handling equipment, expanding our international presence, and advancing our
engineering and manufacturing capabilities to create sustainable long-term value for all our
stakeholders.”
H1FY27 Highlights
Interim Dividend: Declared an interim dividend of Re. 0.50/- (i.e. 50%) per equity share of face
value of Re. 1/- each
Credit Ratings Update: Long Term moved up from [ICRA] AA (Stable) to [ICRA] AA (Positive), and
Short Term reaffirmed to ST: [ICRA] A1+
Collateral Security Release: SBI Bank (Lead Banker) has released Collateral Security for Fund
Based and Non-Fund Based Working Capital Limits. The Hypothecation of movable and immovable
Fixed Assets incl. Plant & Machineries are now removed
Secured Export Orders by MHE: Apart from Gear division, now MHE division has entered into
global market with strong orders of approximately $ 9 Mn

About Elecon Engineering Company Limited:
Elecon Engineering Company Limited (ELECON) was established in 1951 and is one of the
largest manufacturers of Industrial Gears and Material Handling Equipment with over
seven decades of experience and expertise in Asia. The company has been able to
establish its position as one of Asia’s largest and India’s largest Industrial Gear
Manufacturing Company, having manufacturing facility spread over 3,35,000 Square
Meter. The company has a strong global presence serving 95+ countries through a
network of distributors, dealers and customer representatives . The product solutions
include designing, manufacturing, supply, erection and commissioning of the products
and are majorly used in Cement, Sugar, Defense, Steel, Mining and Power sector along
with other sectors
